question: The rupee was ________ relative to other currencies in 1991 as a quick fix to the balance of payment crisis.
solution:
The correct answer is **Devalued**

__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__** Economic Reform of 1991

__
 
• India experienced a severe financial crisis in 1991. A critical Balance of Payments issue started the crisis. The crisis was used as a wonderful chance to overhaul the economy of the nation, its structure, and to implement significant reforms in economic policy.
 
• Stabilization measures and structural changes were implemented by the administration. The former was intended to reduce rigidities in the various Indian economic sectors, whereas the latter was intended to address vulnerabilities that had surfaced on the fiscal and BoP fronts.
 
• P V Narasimha Rao was India's Prime Minister at the time the New Economic Policy (NEP) was unveiled, and Dr. Manmohan Singh was the Finance Minister.

​ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

Monetary Measurements

*In 1991, the rupee's value devalued. The currency rate was the subject of the new government's first significant move.*

 
• Devaluation of the rupee: On July 1, 1991, the government and Reserve Bank of India (RBI) began a two-step devaluation of the rupee. The first devaluation was around 9% versus major currencies, and the second was about 11% two days later.
 
• Over 47 tonnes of gold were sent by the Reserve Bank of India to the Bank of England. It served as collateral for India's request for loans from Japan and England for foreign exchange.
 
• In order to obtain foreign money, the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) simultaneously sold about 20 tonnes of gold to a Swiss bank. Nevertheless, there was a catch—the gold had to be bought back after six months.
 
• The government used a variety of financial techniques to reduce the imports. This reduced some of the burden from currency fluctuations.

*Hence, it can be concluded that the correct answer is option 1. *
